item.title: Charlie Kirk shot dead: FBI director Kash Patel says person detained from scene released; investigation continues
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel announced the release of a subject detained following the shooting of Charlie Kirk at Utah University. The elderly individual was interrogated by law enforcement but later released as the investigation continues. Kirk was shot in the neck while speaking at an event, with police suspecting the shot originated from approximately 200 yards away.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Highway horror in Mexico: 58 injured, 19 critical after gas truck leak sparks massive blast - chilling video
item.description: A gas leak from a tanker truck in Mexico City ignited a massive explosion under a highway overpass, injuring at least 58 people. The blast occurred in Iztapalapa, engulfing vehicles and causing widespread panic. Investigations are underway to determine the cause of the accident, with 19 of the injured in critical condition due to severe burns. Firefighters extinguished the inferno, but emergency crews remain on alert.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump ally Charlie Kirk killed: 10 key points about the shooting
item.description: Charlie Kirk, the founder of Turning Point USA, was fatally shot at a speaking event at Utah Valley University, sparking widespread condemnation and reigniting debates about political violence. The incident, witnessed by hundreds, prompted a campus lockdown and a massive search for the suspect, who remains at large.

item.title: Conservative activist Charlie Kirk shot dead: Trump orders flags half-mast - latest developments
item.description: Conservative activist Charlie Kirk was fatally shot during a speaking event at Utah Valley University, prompting a campus lockdown and a widespread search for the suspect. President Trump mourned Kirk's death, ordering flags to be flown at half-mast. The incident sparked condemnation from political leaders across the spectrum, highlighting concerns about political violence.

item.title: Shot fired from a building 200 yards away? No clarity on shooter after Charlie Kirk dies from bullet injury
item.description: Conservative activist Charlie Kirk tragically died from a gunshot wound sustained during a tour stop at Utah Valley University. The shooting occurred while Kirk was addressing a question about mass shootings and transgender individuals. Confusion surrounds the shooter's identity and location, with conflicting reports about an arrest and whether the shooter was inside the event or nearby.

item.title: Who is Charlie Kirk? Trump ally and right-wing activist shot during Utah campus event; Know all about him
item.description: Conservative activist Charlie Kirk was shot Wednesday at Utah Valley University during an event. Kirk, CEO of Turning Point USA, sustained a gunshot wound near his neck and is in critical condition. Authorities have a suspect in custody following the incident at the Sorensen Center courtyard. Trump urged prayers for Kirk.

item.title: Spreading ‘myths’: Russia says Poland’s drone attack claims are without evidence; accuses of escalating Ukraine crisis
item.description: Russia denies targeting Poland after Warsaw reported shooting down drones that violated its airspace during an attack on Ukraine, accusing Poland of spreading "myths" and failing to provide evidence. Poland invoked NATO's Article 4, calling for consultations on its security, with the Prime Minister stating the country is closer to conflict than any time since World War II.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Optimism fading': Israeli official question success of strike on Qatar; Hamas leaders reportedly survive
item.description: Israeli officials are increasingly doubtful about the success of an airstrike in Qatar targeting Hamas leaders, despite initial optimism. The strike, aimed at disrupting a potential ceasefire proposal, may not have killed the intended high-ranking targets. While Hamas claims its leaders survived, the attack has drawn international condemnation and raised concerns about regional stability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What to know about Qatar, the Middle East's quiet power
item.description: Qatar, a hereditary monarchy enriched by fossil fuels, navigates a complex role in the Middle East. It balances its position as a global conflict mediator with criticisms of human rights abuses and investments in soft power through sports and media. The nation's strategic location and wealth have shaped its history and continue to influence its international relations.

item.title: Belgium seeks US support to battle drug smuggling
item.description: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever has urged the United States to bolster support in combating transnational drug smuggling, particularly at the port of Antwerp. De Wever praised the previous US administration's efforts in targeting drug cartels and seeks enhanced cooperation and information sharing between Europe and the US.

item.title: Who is Larry Ellison: Richest man in the world with more than $393 billion net worth
item.description: Lari Ellison, the Oracle co-founder, is now the world's richest person. His wealth reached $393 billion in 2025. Oracle's stock increased due to AI cloud contracts. This growth helped Ellison surpass Elon Musk. Oracle's focus on AI and cloud services drove this success. Ellison also has investments in Paramount Skydance. He previously served on Tesla's board.

item.title: UAE: 11 illegal domestic worker recruitment offices shut down in Al Ain for licensing violations
item.description: The UAE's Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE), with ADRA, shut down 11 unlicensed domestic worker offices in Al Ain for legal violations. MoHRE warns against illegal hiring, especially via social media, stressing legal, safety, and financial risks. It urges families to use only licensed agencies, now totaling 128 nationwide, to ensure safe, lawful recruitment.
